objective: Find a causally active sparse architecture with high information per GPU-hour before granting long training.

why_changed.current_route_reliance_summary: usually below one absolute accuracy point and below 0.005 in recent temperature/noise screens
why_changed.inference: long training mainly improves shared representations while most tested routers remain weakly causal

prospective_allocation.finish_existing: only healthy jobs already near a declared checkpoint; validate and release
prospective_allocation.do_not_restart: stalled or failed 60/90-epoch exploratory arms solely for matrix completion

stages.question: At which of the 12 FFNs do training-experiment gradients reproducibly conflict?
stages.comparisons: highest-conflict layer or layers versus a low-conflict placebo

stages.question: Can routing become causally active before the shared backbone dominates?

stages.continue_if: noncollapsed routing and either paired OOD/tail movement or strong causal mechanism evidence

continue_to_30_if.accuracy_route: at least +2 OOD-validation points versus the proper dense comparator with no worst-experiment loss, or a predeclared worst-experiment improvement
continue_to_30_if.mechanism_route: route reliance at least 0.01, at least two materially used experts, and reproducible cross-experiment gradient-conflict reduction
continue_to_30_if.id_retention: no more than 2 absolute ID points lost

first_three_bounded_questions: Does conflict-localized placement beat arbitrary early/middle/late placement?
Does replacing two measured conflict-peak FFNs create a materially stronger routing effect than replacing one FFN?
Does staged upcycling create route reliance and expert specialization without erasing Cell-DINO representations?
fairness: Every sparse arm has a placement-, objective-, data-order-, and budget-matched dense control; exact-total-parameter and active-compute claims remain separate.
multiplicity: All discovery screens are exploratory; a winner is locked before fresh-seed confirmation.
